Subject: On-prem / air-gapped deployment — post-call follow-up and next steps

Hi Carlos / team,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation and helpful to hear about the air-gapped requirements up front. Per our call, I wanted to recap the items we discussed and capture the open questions so we can scope an on-prem deployment and an air-gapped upgrade/runbook.

Recap / what we heard
- You require a fully air-gapped Private deployment (no outbound internet from inference nodes).
- Primary workloads: document understanding + secure redaction for regulated products.
- Expected steady-state throughput: ~20 concurrent sessions, 1k tokens/sec aggregate (subject to profiling).
- Maintenance windows: weeknights 12:00–03:00 local, leadership approvals required for any longer windows.

Attachments I’m including:
- onprem-checklist.pdf (initial checklist for network, storage, and hardware)
- network-diagram.drawio (template for your network team to sketch NAT/firewall topology)

Open questions / items we need from you
1) Hardware inventory: list of GPU types and counts (for sizing recommendations). If you have preferred instance types (e.g., A100 80GB), call that out.
2) Upgrade policy: in an air-gapped environment, do you prefer: (A) signed offline bundles delivered via secure transfer/USB, or (B) temporary outbound for package pull during approved maintenance windows?
3) Key management: do you have a customer-managed HSM/KMS (PKCS#11) for model and config encryption, or will Redwood manage keys?
4) Network constraints: any strict firewall/NAT rules, egress restrictions, or proxy requirements for the control plane?
5) Security/compliance contacts: primary person for SOC2 evidence and penetration test coordination.

Proposed next steps
- Please send the hardware inventory and a high-level network diagram to this thread.
- Rishi (cc’d) — our SE — will propose a technical deep dive (we should include your infra and security folks).
- Sign the attached NDA (if needed) — we can also ingest your vendor questionnaire once we complete the tech deep dive.

If the above looks good I’ll set up the tech deep dive for early next week. Thanks again, and let me know if I missed anything.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A couple quick answers and I attached a preliminary network diagram from our infra team.

Answers
- Hardware inventory: currently running a mix: 4 x NVIDIA A100 80GB (in our primary inference cluster) and 6 x A40/RTX6000 class for lower-priority workloads. We’re planning a refresh in Q3 so recommendations that accommodate both are helpful.
- Upgrade policy: our preference is signed offline bundles (option A). We cannot open outbound connections from the inference VLAN except in exceptional cases (requires security approval).
- KMS/HSM: we have a Thales HSM cluster and can expose PKCS#11 to the application host. We’ll need the integration details.
- Network constraints: strict egress rules; only management subnet can reach external endpoints via a jumpbox. Inference nodes sit in isolated VLANs.
- Security contact: it@legacybank.com (copied) — they’ll coordinate evidence requests.

I attached: network-diagram.drawio and a very small hardware inventory spreadsheet (please advise if you need a different format).

We’d like to understand how Redwood handles offline model/package delivery, verification, and rollback in an air-gapped environment. Also SLA and support for emergency fixes in private deployments — can you cover that in the tech deep dive?

Hi Carlos — quick technical notes ahead of the deep dive to make it productive.

Offline/air-gap model & package delivery
- We deliver signed tarball bundles (SHA256 + vendor signature). For air-gapped installs customers pull via a secure SFTP server or provide a USB/secure courier; we verify signatures locally before install.
- Bundles include: runtime container images (OCI tarballs), model artifacts, config manifests, and a signed release manifest with pre/post hooks for validation.

Upgrade/rollback approach
- Upgrades are atomic at the service-group level. We stage the new bundle to a staging node, run smoke tests (locally), then flip traffic with a controlled cutover. Rollback is supported by reapplying the previous signed bundle — we keep a configurable retention of prior artifacts.
- For strict air-gapped sites we provide an offline acceptance test checklist that your infra team can run during the maintenance window (we can automate many checks via the runbook).

HSM/KMS
- We support PKCS#11-based HSMs (Thales, Luna) and have documentation for mounting and key wrapping. Customer-managed keys are supported; Redwood can also provide envelope-wrapping guidance if needed.

Driver / GPU constraints
- Supported GPUs: A100 (40/80GB), A30/A40, and RTX-class for lower-throughput. Recommended baseline for your stated load: minimum 2 x A100 80GB per inference service-group for low-latency production; scale horizontally for throughput. We’ll validate this in profiling.
- We require specific NVIDIA drivers + CUDA versions (we’ll list exact versions for your infra team in the deep dive slides).

Support & emergency fixes
- For Private deployments we offer a paid emergency patch option where we prepare a signed hotfix bundle and coordinate delivery via a secure channel. SLA terms depend on contract tier — we’ll include options in the procurement checklist.

Pre-call ask (tiny)
- If possible, please share the exact driver versions on your A100 nodes and whether the nodes have internet access via the management jumpbox (even if temporarily allowed during a window).

I’ll bring a short demo of the offline bundle verification and the runbook flow to the session. Looking forward to the deep dive — once you confirm a time Marissa will send the invite.

Thanks,
